slices.behaviour: First in this record because its checks are the oldest of this attempt, and it belongs to no slice: it is the fourth review's four findings, of which one was in the deliverable and three were not. The staged run reads NUL-delimited paths into three arrays with read -r -d '', the extension decides which array a path joins in a case rather than a regex over a flattened string, and each tool is handed "${array[@]}", so a staged path with a space reaches Biome, ast-grep and dependency-cruiser whole; the two shellcheck disable=SC2086 comments are gone with the splitting they excused, and so is the keep helper, which existed only to filter the flattened list (F21). The knip fixture computes integer cents, Math.round((amountCents * 15) / 100) in both of its functions, so commissionCents(1001) is 150 rather than 150.15 (F20); nothing tests a fixture's incidental arithmetic on purpose, and all twenty-three rules still refuse their own fixture after it, 23 of 23 at check 282. And the ticket file is corrected twice: the paragraph predicting the doctor warning no longer says how many findings name the candidate, for the same reason the weekly figures are not quoted, because report.rule_loop counts them from the journal on the day it is asked (F18), and the deferred typecheck paragraph's figure for the six test files now names the check that printed it, 122 diagnostics at check 277 (F19).
slices.failure_reason: With scripts/rules.sh back at its committed version and a violating packages/core/src/violation with space.ts staged, three of the sixty tests of harness/tests/test_rules.py failed. StagedPathWithASpaceTest.test_the_staged_run_refuses_a_violation_in_a_path_with_a_space failed with "AssertionError: 'violation with space.ts' not found in" the script's own output, which read 'Checked 0 files in 231ms. No fixes applied.' and 'biome: ok in 0s', then 'ast-grep: ok in 0s', and then dependency-cruiser refusing three paths that do not exist, 'packages/core/src/violation', 'with' and 'space.ts', each 'No such file or directory (os error 2)'. The script did exit 1, which is why the first assertion passed, but it exited on dependency-cruiser's internal errors over the fragments of one path rather than on the euro sign the fixture carries, and the rule scoped to that path, ast-grep/no-euro-sign, reported ok having read nothing. The two cheap tests that read the script failed beside it: test_the_staged_run_hands_each_tool_only_the_staged_paths with "AssertionError: '\"${code_paths[@]}\"' not found in" run_staged, and test_the_staged_run_never_word_splits_its_path_list with "AssertionError: '$code_paths' unexpectedly found in" the same function.

That the hook calls the runner on the staged paths and never on the tree, that the staged mode hands each tool only those paths and runs knip in neither, that every tool goes through timed so the ten-second budget is measured on every commit, that CI runs rules --check, rules --fixtures and the tree run, and that all seven packages declare an exports map.
